title: How annual pre-pay creates an infinite marketing budget: payback math and cash-flow
summary: Jason Cohen shows how to compute the real payback period of a SaaS customer (CAC / (MRR × GPM)) and why fast growth eats cash. Annual prepay plans collect a year of revenue up front, so ad spend on a credit card is repaid before the bill is due, transforming bootstrapped cash-flow. He also ranks levers: raise prices first, cut costs last.

principles.text: Compute the cost to create $1 of MRR (CAC / ARPC); the number is usually eye-opening.
principles.quote: The cost to create one more dollar of `MRR` = `CAC / ARPC`

principles.text: Real payback must be measured on gross-margin dollars, not revenue: p = CAC / (MRR × GPM).
Faster growth consumes more cash because every dollar spent takes the full payback period to return.
principles.quote: And **the faster you grow the more cash it takes**, because no matter how much you spend, it still takes a year to get it back.

principles.text: Pricing and marketing are uncapped strategic levers; cost-cutting is capped, so don't let engineers default to it.
principles.quote: Remember, you can only cut costs so much, but the potential upside of better marketing or pricing is uncapped.

principles.text: Launch an annual plan at 12x the current monthly price, then raise monthly about 20%; it's a natural excuse to lift prices.
principles.quote: Offer the annual plan at 12 times the _current_ monthly price, then increase the month-to-month price by something like 20%

principles.text: Annual prepay lets you collect the customer's year of cash before the ad bill comes due, removing the cash drag of acquisition.
principles.quote: We received the $80 from the customer _before_ we sent away the $80 for the ad, even after setting aside `GPM` costs.
